record.original_question: Let (Omega, mu) be a sigma-finite measure space, let V be a dense subspace of L2(Omega), and let a: V x V -> C be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form. Let A be the associated operator on L2(Omega), so that -A generates a bounded analytic semigroup (T(t)) on L2(Omega). If L-infinity-boundedness means that there exists M > 0 such that ||T(t)f||_infinity <= M ||f||_infinity for all f in L2(Omega) intersect L-infinity(Omega) and all t >= 0, can this L-infinity-boundedness property be characterized directly in terms of the sesquilinear form a?

evidence.quote: The semigroup (T (t))t≥0 is called L∞ -bounded, if there exists M > 0 such that kT (t)f k∞ ≤ Mkf k∞ , for all f ∈ L2 (Ω) ∩ L∞ (Ω).
Can L∞ -boundedness of (T (t))t≥0 be characterized in terms of the sesquilinear form a?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and let $V$ be a dense subspace of $L^2(\Omega)$. Let $a\colon V\times V\to\mathbb{C}$ be a closed sectorial sesquilinear form, i.e., there exist $\omega\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\theta\in[0,\pi/2)$ such that
$$|\operatorname{Im} a(u,u)|\le \tan(\theta)\,(\operatorname{Re} a(u,u)+\omega\|u\|_2^2)\qquad(u\in V),$$
and $V$ endowed with the inner product $\operatorname{Re} a(u,v)+(\omega+1)(u,v)_{L^2}$ is complete. Let $A$ be the operator on $L^2(\Omega)$ associated to $a$ via the first representation theorem, so that $-A$ generates a bounded analytic semigroup $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ on $L^2(\Omega)$.

Say that $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ is $L^\infty$-bounded if there exists $M>0$ such that
$$\|T(t)f\|_\infty\le M\,\|f\|_\infty\qquad\text{for all }f\in L^2(\Omega)\cap L^\infty(\Omega)\text{ and all }t\ge 0.$$

Problem: Give a characterization of the $L^\infty$-boundedness of $(T(t))_{t\ge 0}$ directly in terms of the sesquilinear form $a$ (analogous to the Beurling–Deny–Ouhabaz type criteria for $L^\infty$-contractivity, positivity, or invariance of closed convex sets).
artifact.status_search_result: The $L^\infty$-contractivity case (with constant $M=1$) is characterized by Ouhabaz's invariance criterion via the form, but the general $L^\infty$-boundedness case (with arbitrary constant $M$) is not known to admit such a form-theoretic characterization. Available literature on sesquilinear forms and semigroup invariance/domination addresses contractivity but does not provide a characterization for mere boundedness, so the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Sectorial forms and degenerate differential operators
status_evidence.snippet: Theory of sesquilinear forms and m-sectorial operators, including invariance criteria.
status_evidence.claim: The standard form-theoretic invariance criteria (Beurling–Deny–Ouhabaz) address L^infty-contractivity, not mere L^infty-boundedness.

status_evidence.title: Invariance of closed convex sets and domination criteria for semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Ouhabaz's criterion characterizes invariance of closed convex sets (and hence L^infty-contractivity) of a semigroup generated by a sesquilinear form.
status_evidence.claim: Existing characterizations concern contractivity, leaving the boundedness question without a known form-based characterization.
